title: Two-way Magnetic Resonance Tuning Nanoprobe Enhanced Subtraction Imaging for Precision Diagnosis of Brain Metastasis
text:
Accurate diagnosis and assessment of brain metastases in patients with systemic cancers has important
implications for patient prognosis and treatment strategy. The proposed two-way magnetic resonance tuning
nanoprobes and complementary subtraction imaging technology with ultra-high tumor-to-normal tissue ratios will
provide neuroradiology practice with a highly capable, accurate and consistent approach for detecting and
evaluating early brain metastases. This new imaging technology has great potential to be translated in clinic to
improve survival and reduce the mortality rate in patients with brain metastases in the near future.

title: Project 2: Combinatorial Intralesional Studies of Immune Checkpoints Inhibition
text:
Project 2 will evaluate how combinations of immune checkpoint modulators delivered systemically or locally via
an oncolytic virus can improve therapy against immune checkpoint resistant GBM mouse models and determine
via T cell gene editing the signaling pathways that are important for effective immune rejection. These studies
will inform how best we can overcome GBM’s evasion from immunotherapy.

title: Mechanism and Regulation of Replication-Coupled Asymmetric Histone Incorporation in Drosophila Male Germline Stem Cells
text:
The proper maintenance of “immortal” cell populations like adult stem cells is important to prevent cell overproliferation
(cancer) or cell degeneration and loss (premature aging). Adult stem cells in both humans and flies undergo asymmetric cell
division to maintain stem cells while creating differentiating cells, and epigenetics underlie these different cell fate decisions.
Here I propose studying the role of chromatin and DNA replication timing on asymmetric histone incorporation to better
understand how epigenetic asymmetry can be established and regulated to produce substantially different cell fates and
ensure proper cell maintenance and homeostasis.

title: A novel universal Treg therapy via ICAM-1 specific chimeric antigen receptor to suppress ischemia reperfusion injury and alloimmunity
text:
In this project, we develop an autologous and universal, HLA-independent CAR Tregs therapy to target ischemia
reperfusion injury in deceased organ transplants. The utility of HLA-targeted CAR Tregs, is hampered by
unknown donor-recipient HLA-matching in cases of deceased organ transplantation. We generate a fourth-
generation CAR-Treg that targets a universal antigen, ICAM, that is highly expressed in ischemia reperfusion.

title: Deciphering the function of the APE2 nuclease during repair by alternative end-joining and its role in HR-deficient cells
text:
Cancer cells that are deficient in homologous recombination (HR) rely on an alternative pathway,
Alt-EJ, to repair DNA breaks induced by replication. As a consequence, inhibition of Alt-EJ is
lethal in these cancers, and could be used as a therapeutic approach to eliminate HR-deficient
cancers. We have identified the nuclease APE2 as an uncharacterized central player of Alt-EJ,
and we will determine its molecular function and its potential as a novel therapeutic target.

title: AI-driven Multimodal Model for PrEP Candidacy Assessment in Women (AiM-PrEP)
text:
Women in the Southern US have a significantly lower rate of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake for HIV
prevention than men. Electronic health record (EHR)-based machine learning models have been used
effectively to identify candidates for PrEP within health systems but have performance limitations in women;
these limitations can potentially be addressed by incorporating neighborhood-level data on social context into
the models. The AI-Driven Multimodal Modelling for PrEP Candidacy for Women Study (AIM-PrEP), will
develop, implement and evaluate a societal context-informed, AI-driven clinical tool to assist primary care
providers in efficiently identifying women who can benefit from PrEP.

title: Evaluation of novel microscale cell culture platform for translational drug development in prostate cancer
text:
Prostate cancer is a disease with a remarkably high impact on Veteran health. Not only is it the most common
cancer diagnosed in Veterans, with nearly 15,000 new cases diagnosed each year, but Veteran men get
diagnosed with prostate cancer at nearly twice the rate of the general population. Unfortunately, even with
treatment, many of these Veterans will eventually die from their prostate cancer. New, effective prostate cancer
treatments are therefore desperately needed. While this research begins in the lab, current laboratory research
models do a notoriously poor job of identifying therapies that will be effective in patients. We have therefore
developed a new cell culture platform, called Stacks, that enables improved modeling of patient tumors in the
lab using their own cells. Our primary objective in the proposal will be to determine whether the Stacks platform
can better mirror the biology inside patient tumors and more accurately predict the effectiveness of prostate
cancer therapies in Veteran men with metastatic prostate cancer than currently available platforms.

title: Next-generation genetic engineering of the pan-leukocyte antigen CD45 to facilitate CAR-T cell therapy against hematologic malignancies
text:
(PROJECT 2) 
This proposal seeks to bring the power of genetically-modified T cell therapy to the treatment of patients with 
AML using cutting edge genetic engineering approaches. The proposed research is relevant to public health 
because it addresses the challenges facing physician-scientists in the quest to find and use cancer-specific 
antigens for immunotherapy and is relevant to those parts of the NCI’s mission that pertain to eliminating 
suffering and death due to cancer. This work is expected to open new therapeutic horizons in the field of 
adoptive immunotherapy for AML and new research horizons that could be translated to other malignancies by 
combining CART cell therapy with gene editing.

title: Targeting the SKP2 Axis for Anti-melanoma Therapy
text:
The proposed study aims to develop novel therapeutic strategies for treating melanoma with elevated oncogenic
SKP2 and Hedgehog signaling pathways. Identification of the melanoma pathogenesis-relevant RNF12-SKP2-
HHIP signaling axis will provide prognostic biomarkers as well as the molecular basis for developing SKP2
targeted therapy and cancer immunotherapy for the better treatment of patients with melanoma.

title: Airway inflammation and fear: elucidating immune mediators and neural substrates
text:
Abnormal fear regulation is observed in psychiatric disorders, particularly PTSD, a debilitating condition afflicting
8% of civilians and about 22% of combat veterans annually. Growing evidence supports an association of
autoimmune conditions and severe asthma with PTSD prevalence and risk, however contributory mechanisms
are not clear. Using cell-circuit approaches and transgenic manipulations, this R01 will identify T cell-derived
inflammatory mediators, cellular substrates and unique forebrain circuits involved in asthma-driven fear
dysregulation relevant to PTSD.

title: Optimizing Use of Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) to Advance Health Equity Among Youth with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D)
text:
The use of personal medical devices (e.g. continuous glucose monitors) by youth with type 1 diabetes as well
as their potential to aid children and their caregivers to manage the daily demands of type 1 diabetes and
optimize blood sugar control have rapidly expanded over the past twenty years. However, demographic (e.g.
race/ethnicity) and socioeconomic (e.g. household income, parental education, and insurance) factors impact
access to and continued use of such technology. The goals of this project are to better describe and analyze
the interplay of such factors in sustained utilization of CGM in different clinical settings and to characterize their
impact on a national level to enable the development and implementation of a pilot study designed to achieve
improved equity in continuous glucose monitoring use for pediatric patients with type 1 diabetes.

title: Identification of Druggable Targets for Cancer Therapy-Induced Cardiotoxicity
text:
Proteasomal inhibitors (PI) are highly effective cancer therapies for blood cancer, yet their usage is cautioned
due to significant cardiovascular side effects. In this proposal, we will investigate the underlying mechanisms of
PI-induced cardiovascular toxicity (PI-CVT) employing a number of state-of-the-art approaches, including iPSC
technologies, tissue engineering, multi-omics, and CRISPR interference/activation for genome-wide screening.
The knowledge we collect here will provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of PI-CVT and enable the
development of molecularly targeted, disease-specific therapeutics to prevent PI-CVT.

title: The molecular gradients underlying wiring plasticity in the visual cortex
text:
It remains a central problem in neuroscience how early postnatal experience sculpts the development of neural
circuits. The objective of this research program is to use the vision-dependent development of mouse visual
cortex as a model system to investigate the molecular and cellular basis of wiring plasticity in the developing
mouse brain using a combination of transcriptomics, epigenomics, connectomics and integrative computational
analysis. Molecular mechanisms of cortical wiring plasticity uncovered in this work will provide insights into how
other sensory experience sculpts brain circuitry, and will provide a foundation towards understanding human
neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: The role of SUV39H1 in maintaining heterochromatin architecture and identity in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
text:
H3K9me3, a histone modification marking heterochromatin, is dysregulated in AML. This proposal
seeks to investigate the role of SUV39H1, the major H3K9me3 depositor, in preserving 3D genome
structure in AML cells and to explore its potential as a therapeutic target alongside FDA-approved
HMA therapy. Successful completion of this study will yield crucial insights into 3D chromatin
organization, offering innovative epigenetic approaches for treating myeloid malignancy.

title: Alpha-emitter Imaging for Dosimetry and Treatment Planning
text:
Quantitative imaging of α-particle emitters is important for dosimetry needed to optimize patient therapy. Well
validated methods for such imaging do not currently exist. We will develop and validate such methods while also
considering different approaches to reduce the number of imaging sessions required for accurate dosimetry of
αRPT

title: Mapping the Human Metabolome Using Synthesis and Mass Spectrometry
text:
The majority of metabolites in the human body remain unknown, yet these metabolites may play a critical role
in important biological mechanisms such as disease pathogenesis. This proposal uses a strategy called
reverse metabolomics, which combines organic synthesis, mass spectrometry and public data mining for the
high-throughput characterization of small molecules in humans. Ultimately, this approach offers insight into new
disease biomarkers, druggable pathways and bioactive small molecules.

title: NextGenSIT: An Off-the-Shelf and On-Demand Product for Biological Control of Aedes aegypti Mosquitoes
text:
The project aims to complete the development, delivery, and deployment of Synvect’s NextGenSIT product,
providing an eco-friendly and cost-effective solution for Aedes aegypti mosquito control. By conducting
semi-field trials and small-scale open-air pilots, the project seeks to validate efficacy while actively engaging
partners and converting them into paying customers, thereby strengthening its go-to-market strategy ahead of
large-scale open-air pilots under an Experimental Use Permit. These efforts will lay the foundation for full
commercialization following U.S. regulatory approval.

title: The study of Eicosanoids as Novel Inflammatory Mediators of CVD in Men and Women with HIV
text:
People with HIV who are treated with antiretroviral therapy suffer from increased heart disease. We will study
specific molecules, namely eicosanoids, to find out if they are involved in the pathway by which persistent
inflammation due to HIV infection may lead to heart disease.

title: Mechanisms of immunosuppression triggered by checkpoint blockade immunotherapy
text:
PD-1-based checkpoint blockade immunotherapy (CBI) provides durable benefits to several patients yet
fails in most of them. One possible reason is that, besides increasing the antitumor efficacy of effector T cells,
CBI may stimulate immunosuppressive mechanisms that promote tumor growth. We propose to identify these
mechanisms, which may vary depending on the characteristics of individual tumors and the type of CBI used.
Our work is instrumental in devising new CBI regimens with increased efficacy against human tumors.

title: Ecological immunology of a flea vector (Ctenocephalides felis)
text:
PROJECT NARATIVE
It has been hypothesized that insect immune responses can be harnessed to control the spread of vector-borne
diseases. Although fleas transmit numerous deadly and debilitating diseases to humans, relatively little is known
about how they defend themselves from infection under natural conditions. The proposed research aims to
address basic entomological questions related to flea ecological immunology, which could aid in the development
of novel control strategies for flea-borne diseases.
